referenceCard.title: Conditionals

subtitle: A program that decides. First True wins; indentation shows what belongs.

teach.body:
A comparison is a question with a True or False answer: 5 > 3 is True, 5 == 3 is False. == asks 'equal?'; = stores a value. Others: != (not equal), <, <=, >, >=.

if condition: runs the indented lines below it only when the condition is True. % gives a remainder, so n % 2 == 0 asks 'is n even?'.
teach.title: Asking a question

teach.body:
if a: … elif b: … else: … is one chain. Python checks a; if it's True, that block runs and the rest of the chain is skipped. Only if a is False does it check b, and so on. else runs when nothing above was True. So at most one block in a chain runs, and order matters.

Two separate if statements are two separate questions; both can run.
teach.title: Chains: first True wins

teach.body:
x and y is True only when both are. x or y is True when at least one is. not x flips it. Python works out the left side first; if that already decides the answer, the right side is skipped (False and … is False whatever follows). Lua's and / or skip the same way.

Indentation is the structure. Lines indented under if belong to it; the first line back at the left edge is outside and always runs.
teach.title: Combining with and, or, not
